policy.discountCaps: Campaign offers ≤20% effective. 25% only on spot offers, annuals, bulk privates and bulk purchases. Intro products (3-for-2, credited passes, gift cards) are acquisition cost and convert into memberships at ≤20% effective.
policy.stacking: Campaign offers replace — never add to — the standing 15% newcomer/lapsed perk unless the offer says 'standard 15%'. Non-price perks (days, freezes, guest passes, retail) may sit on top of a discount.

journeys.Mumbai: Barre: free trial. Strength Lab and powerCycle: Newcomers 2-for-1. All three formats at Kwality and Supreme HQ.

journeys.Pop-ups: Barre/Pilates partner venues (Copper + Cloves, Plash Pilates). Paid trial class.

policy.discountDefinition: effective% = the cash discount plus the list value of any non-cash perks (extra days, freezes, guest passes, privates, retail), valued at the studio’s own catalogue price. Cash alone is capped at 20%, except spot offers, annuals, bulk privates, bulk purchases and credited intro products, which may reach 25% (and, for credited intro products, whatever the acquisition cost works out to).

offerBank.name: The 57-Hour Hangover Sale
offerBank.offerDetails: 1 Month Unlimited at a flat ₹15,000 in Mumbai (list ₹20,239, 26% off) or ₹10,000 at Kenkere (list ₹14,595, 31% off). Fri 1 Jan 00:00 to Sun 3 Jan 09:00 — 57 hours. Capped at 57 memberships per city, 1 per person, activate by 15 Jan.
offerBank.headline: Hungover? Same. 1 month unlimited, flat ₹15,000. 57 hours only.
offerBank.customerMessage: Hungover? Same. For the next 57 hours, 1 Month Unlimited is a flat ₹15,000 (Bengaluru: ₹10,000). Only 57 memberships per city, then it disappears faster than your NYE plans. Start any day before 15 Jan.
offerBank.commercialJob: Front-load January cash and capture the resolution spike before it cools.
offerBank.logic: January is the strongest non-April month in Mumbai (Jan-26: Kwality ₹27.4L, Bandra ₹20.0L; Kenkere ₹11.1L). A capped spot price creates urgency without training clients to wait — only 57 units per city, so the maximum discount exposure is ~₹3.0L in Mumbai and ~₹2.6L in Bengaluru.
offerBank.rules: Spot offer, so the >25% cap does not apply. Replaces (does not stack with) the 15% newcomer or lapsed perk. Active members may buy it as their next renewal only if their plan ends before 31 Jan.
offerBank.kpi: Sell-out time; share of spot buyers renewing in Feb at standard price (target 55%).

offerBank.name: Third Time's the Charm
offerBank.offerDetails: Replaces the Newcomers 2-for-1 for January. Mumbai: 3 classes for ₹3,885 (price of 2 singles) — mix barre, powerCycle and Strength Lab (Lab seats at Supreme HQ; Kwality off-peak only), use within 14 days. Kenkere: 3 barre classes for ₹2,835 (counts as the once-in-a-lifetime 2-for-1; replaces the 50% intro in January). Then the standard 15% on a first membership: 1 Month ₹17,203 / ₹12,406.
offerBank.headline: First class: awkward. Second: better. Third: hooked. 3 classes for the price of 2.
offerBank.customerMessage: First class: awkward. Second class: better. Third class: you're hooked. Try barre, powerCycle and Strength Lab — 3 classes for the price of 2 (₹3,885). Bengaluru: 3 barre classes for ₹2,835. Love it? Your first membership is 15% off.
offerBank.commercialJob: Lift trial-to-member conversion by getting newcomers to the 3-visit mark.
offerBank.logic: 60.6% of first-timers never take a 2nd class. Purchase within 60 days by month-1 visits: 0 return visits 10.8%, 1 → 43.9%, 2 → 73.3%, 3–4 → 88.6%. The 2-for-1 route converts 20.8% (Bandra 17%). A third class moves people into the 73–89% band.
offerBank.rules: One per person (phone verified). Intro products sit outside the 25% cap as acquisition cost. Class 2 booked at the desk before leaving class 1.
offerBank.kpi: Packs with all 3 classes used in 14 days (target 60%); pack → membership (target 35% vs 20.8% on 2-for-1).

offerBank.name: The Baker's Dozen
offerBank.offerDetails: Annual Unlimited at 15% off — Mumbai ₹1,86,533 (list ₹2,19,450), Kenkere ₹1,32,804 (list ₹1,56,240) — for 13 months instead of 12, plus the standard annual perks (2 privates, 4 guest passes, 1 hosted class, monthly trainer check-ins).
offerBank.headline: 12 months is so 2026. Renew your annual and get 13.
offerBank.customerMessage: 12 months is so 2026. Renew your annual this January and we'll bake in a 13th month — plus your 2 privates, 4 guest passes, a hosted class and monthly trainer check-ins. A baker's dozen hits different.
offerBank.commercialJob: Re-up the annuals that fall due in Dec–Feb and upgrade 3M/6M members to annual.
offerBank.logic: Annual is Kwality's #1 product (32 units, ₹51.6L in the last 12 months) and Bandra's #3 (15 units, ₹23.8L). The ANN-2026-25%-KH code gave away ₹9.7L at a flat 25%; this gives less cash away (≈21.5% effective) and adds time, which costs little at spare capacity.
offerBank.rules: ≈21.5% effective (annual cap 25%). Annual, 6M and 3M members expiring 1 Dec–28 Feb.
offerBank.kpi: Annual re-up rate (target 75%); 3M/6M → annual upgrades.

offerBank.name: U Up? It's 2027.
offerBank.offerDetails: Lapsed 61–365 days: the standard 15% on 1 Month (₹17,203 / ₹12,406) or a 12-class pack (₹16,735 / ₹11,156). Take 12 classes by 31 Jan and get +5 days (pack buyers: +1 class). Pop-ups: 15% on an 8- or 10-class pack (₹5,891 / ₹7,229) and +1 class for 6 classes by 31 Jan.
offerBank.headline: U up? Your mat's been asking about you.
offerBank.customerMessage: U up? Your mat's been asking about you. Come back this January: 15% off, and hit 12 classes this month for 5 bonus days. No awkward small talk, promise.
offerBank.commercialJob: Reactivate lapsed clients in the highest-intent month and get them active before February’s Valentine’s season.
offerBank.logic: Bandra is reactivation-led (3,209 lapsed vs 5,065 renewed membership records). Renewal climbs with usage: Bandra members using <50% of sessions renew 49–58% vs 82% at 75%+. The bonus is only paid for attendance that predicts the next renewal.
offerBank.rules: Standard lapsed 15%, bonus earned (≈20% effective if earned). No stacking with the spot sale.
offerBank.kpi: Lapsed buyers; share hitting 12 classes (target 40%); Feb renewal of Jan winbacks.

offerBank.name: Blind Date (No Catfishing)
offerBank.offerDetails: Mumbai: 2 mystery classes in 10 days for ₹999. The format (Barre, powerCycle or Strength Lab) and the trainer stay sealed in an envelope until you walk in; date two is booked at the desk before you leave. Kenkere: 2 mystery Barre classes (trainer and playlist sealed) for ₹709. Pop-ups: the paid trial (≈₹945), with the second class free if it is booked at the desk. Buy within 72 hours of date two and the ₹999 / ₹709 is credited against 1 Month at the standard 15% (₹16,204 / ₹11,697 net). Pop-ups: 8-class pack at 15% (₹5,891).
offerBank.headline: Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.
offerBank.customerMessage: Blind date, but the only red flag is our grip socks. Two mystery classes for ₹999 (Kenkere ₹709): you find out the format and the trainer at the door. Like what you see? We credit the full ₹999 against your first month.
offerBank.commercialJob: Turn Valentine’s-season curiosity into first memberships without a 50% code.
offerBank.logic: Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.
offerBank.rules: One per phone number. The intro fee is credited only within 72 hours of class 2. Standard 15% only; no stacking.
offerBank.kpi: Second-date booked at the desk (target 70%); trial → member (target 30%).

offerBank.name: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind)
mechanicTags: pays only on a new buyer
offerBank.offerDetails: Every active member gets three printed love letters at the desk (and a WhatsApp version). Each one gives a never-been friend 2 free classes within 14 days. If the friend buys 1 Month or a 12-class pack within 72 hours of class 2: their standard 15% (₹17,203 / ₹12,406; pop-ups 8-class ₹5,891) plus P57 grip socks, and the member gets +5 days (pack: +1 class) per friend who buys, up to 15 days. Partner Barre on Sun 14 Feb counts as class 2.
offerBank.headline: Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.
offerBank.customerMessage: Love bombing, but healthy: write a friend a love letter at the desk and they get 2 classes on us. If they join, they get 15% off and grip socks, and you get 5 extra days. Three letters, three chances.
offerBank.commercialJob: Turn members into recruiters; only pay when a new person buys.
offerBank.logic: Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.
offerBank.rules: The friend must be new to P57 (phone verified). Member reward: +5 days per buying friend, max 15. Standard 15% for the friend only.
offerBank.kpi: Letters redeemed; new buyers from referral (target +40% vs Feb-26).

offerBank.name: Put a Ring On It
offerBank.offerDetails: Any February renewal: 3 Months at 15% (₹49,177 / ₹35,879) + a P57 mini-band “ring”; 6 Months at 15% + 1 private session (₹96,658 / ₹69,883); Annual at the standard 20% + the annual perks + your name engraved on the Wall of Commitment. Say yes at the desk and the bell rings, confetti, the class applauds. Pop-ups: 10-class pack at 10% + the mini-band (₹7,655).
offerBank.headline: If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.
offerBank.customerMessage: If you like it, put a ring on it: renew for 3 months at 15% and get the ring (a mini-band, relax), 6 months at 15% with a private, or go annual and get your name on the Wall of Commitment.
offerBank.commercialJob: Move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans with a reason to say yes on the spot.
offerBank.logic: Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.
offerBank.rules: 3M 16.4% / 6M 19.6% effective (perks at list); annual at the standard 20%. One ring per renewal. No stacking.
offerBank.kpi: 3M+ share of renewal value (target 45%); proposals accepted at the desk.

offerBank.name: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule
offerBank.offerDetails: Lapsed 61–365 days pick a relationship status at the standard 15%: Exclusive = 3 Months (₹49,177 / ₹35,879) + 1 extra freeze; Casual = a 12-class pack (₹16,735 / ₹11,156); It’s Complicated = 1 Month (₹17,203 / ₹12,406) + 1 free freeze for the week life gets in the way. Pop-ups: 8-class pack at 15% (₹5,891). Galentine’s class Sat 13 Feb: bring a friend free.
offerBank.headline: It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.
offerBank.customerMessage: It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Come back on your terms: Exclusive (3 months), Casual (12 classes) or It’s Complicated (1 month + a free freeze). 15% off whichever you pick.
offerBank.commercialJob: Bring lapsed clients back by letting them choose the commitment.
offerBank.logic: Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
offerBank.rules: Lapsed 61–365 days. Standard lapsed 15% only; freezes have no cash value.
offerBank.kpi: Reactivations; mix of Exclusive / Casual / Complicated (target 30% Exclusive).

offerBank.name: Monogamy Is Overrated
offerBank.offerDetails: For members who've used one format in the last 60 days. Pack members renew at list and get 2 bonus classes valid only in formats they've never tried (Mumbai: powerCycle / Strength Lab induction / Cardio Barre; Kenkere: Cardio Barre / Mat 57 / Foundations). Unlimited members renew at list and get +5 days if they take 3 different formats in their first 30 days.
offerBank.headline: Committed to one class? Cute. Members who play the field stay longer.
offerBank.customerMessage: Committed to one class? Cute. Members who play the field stay longer — so renew this month and we'll pay for your next two flings: 2 bonus classes in formats you've never tried.
offerBank.commercialJob: Lift renewal rates by widening each member's format mix.
offerBank.logic: One-format members renew 58–67% vs 85–87% for members on 4+ formats. Bonus classes cost little in off-peak slots and target the single biggest renewal predictor after attendance.
offerBank.rules: No price discount; ≈17% value on a 12-class pack, ≈16% on 1M if the bonus is earned.
offerBank.kpi: Members trying a new format (target 40% of eligible); 60-day renewal of exposed vs unexposed members.

Book a second class before leaving and buy 1 Month or a 12-class pack within 72 hours: the standard 15% (₹17,203 / ₹16,735) plus a free Lab induction seat for a friend.
offerBank.headline: Women's Day isn't about flowers. It's about deadlifts.
offerBank.customerMessage: Women's Day isn't about flowers. It's about deadlifts. Your first Strength Lab class at Supreme HQ is on us, 8–14 March. Bring the attitude; we've got the weights.

offerBank.logic: Bandra's Lab runs ~48% full vs Kwality's 83%, so Kwality is excluded. Strength/powerCycle-first visits convert 20.4% vs barre 25.6% today — this tests whether a free, coached Lab first visit closes that gap.

offerBank.kpi: Lab first visits; Lab-first → purchase vs barre trial (target ≥25%).

offerBank.focus: Women's Day + Main Character Month (format exploration)
offerBank.name: Bura Na Mano, Renewal Hai
offerBank.offerDetails: Holi, Sun 21–Mon 22 Mar (48 hours): 3 Months at 15% off (₹49,177 / ₹35,879) or a 12-class pack at 10% (₹17,719 / ₹11,813), each with a limited-edition 'Holi Hai' P57 tee (retail ≈₹2,000 — confirm).
offerBank.headline: Bura na mano, renewal hai. 48 hours only.
offerBank.customerMessage: Bura na mano, renewal hai. 48 hours only: 3 months at 15% off and a limited-edition Holi tee. Colours wash out. Abs don't.
offerBank.commercialJob: Stop March expiries waiting for April's anniversary pricing.
offerBank.logic: In 2026 Kwality did ₹20.2L in March, then ₹50.0L in April at 20.4% discount depth — March renewals waited. A short, fun window with a 3M upgrade pulls them forward at ≤20% effective.
offerBank.rules: Members expiring 1–31 Mar only. 3M ≈18.5% effective; pack ≈20%.
offerBank.kpi: March renewal yield (target 70%); 3M share of March renewals.

offerBank.focus: Women's Day + Main Character Month (format exploration)
offerBank.name: The Second Date's On Us
offerBank.offerDetails: Kenkere: Newcomers Intro (first class at 50% off, ₹709) → class 2 free if booked at the desk before leaving, within 7 days → 1 Month (₹12,406) or 8-class pack (₹7,408) at the standard 15% within 72 hours of class 2, plus 1 extra freeze. Pop-ups: paid trial (≈₹945) → second class free if booked before leaving → 8- or 10-class pack at 15% within 72 hours.
offerBank.headline: First date: half price. Second date: on us. Third: it's a relationship.
offerBank.customerMessage: First date: half price. Second date: on us. Third date? That's a relationship — 15% off your first month and an extra freeze for when life gets busy.
offerBank.commercialJob: Fix Bengaluru's lead → trial → member leak.
offerBank.logic: Kenkere logged 3,217 leads in 12 months; only 36% reached a trial and 13.1% converted. 581 single-class sales show high drop-in, low commitment. A booked second visit lifts conversion from 10.8% to 43.9%.
offerBank.rules: Standard 15% only; freeze has no cash value.
offerBank.kpi: Second-visit rate (target 55%); trial → member (target 25% vs 18.7%).

offerBank.offerDetails: A 9-Month Unlimited that exists only in April: Mumbai ₹1,44,999 (a 6-Month plus a 3-Month cost ₹1,71,570), Kenkere ₹1,02,999 (₹1,24,425). 9 freezes (min 3 days each), the anniversary hoodie, a numbered brass studio key and your name on the Lease Wall. 99 numbered keys across Kwality and Supreme HQ, 39 at Kenkere; a live counter on the studio screens.
offerBank.headline: Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. 99 keys. No second batch.
offerBank.customerMessage: Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. The 9-Month Lease: 9 months unlimited, 9 freezes, the anniversary hoodie and a numbered brass key. 99 keys in Mumbai, 39 in Bengaluru. When they’re gone, they’re gone.

offerBank.kpi: Keys sold vs 99 / 39; 6M+ share of April membership revenue (target 50%).

offerBank.offerDetails: 9 numbered Annual Unlimited seats per studio at the standard 20% (₹1,75,560 / ₹1,24,992) with the annual perks doubled: 4 privates, 8 guest passes, 2 hosted classes, monthly trainer check-ins, a numbered jacket, your name on the Club Nine wall and 48-hour priority booking all year. Unveiled at the Birthday Bash on Sat 17 Apr.
offerBank.headline: Nine numbered seats per studio. Founder perks for a year.
offerBank.customerMessage: Nine seats. Nine years. Club Nine is an annual membership with the perks doubled: 4 privates, 8 guest passes, priority booking all year and a numbered jacket. Nine per studio, and then the table is full.

offerBank.name: Spin Class (Literally)
offerBank.offerDetails: Renew 1 Month or a 12-class pack in April at 10% off (₹18,215 / ₹17,719; Kenkere ₹13,136 / ₹11,813; pop-up 10-pack ₹7,655) and spin the Wheel of Nine. Published odds: +1 class 30%, smoothie 20%, guest pass 15%, grip socks 10%, +3 days 10%, extra freeze 8%, 30-min private 5%, P57 tote 1.5%, a free month 0.5%. Then choose: keep it, double it by booking 9 classes in your first 21 days, or donate it to a friend as a guest pass.
offerBank.headline: Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.
offerBank.customerMessage: Renew in April and spin the Wheel of Nine: every spin wins. Then decide: keep your prize, double it, or gift it to a friend. Odds are on the wall, because we’re not that kind of casino.
offerBank.commercialJob: Full-price-adjacent renewals with a prize everyone talks about.
offerBank.logic: Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.
offerBank.rules: One spin per renewal; published odds; doubled prizes credited only once the 9 classes are attended. ≈19.5% effective on the expected value.
offerBank.kpi: April renewal yield vs April 2026; share of spins doubled (target 35%).

Kenkere: 3 Barre classes for ₹699 (replaces the 50% intro in April; counts as the once-in-a-lifetime 2-for-1). Pop-ups: 2 classes for ₹999. offerBank.customerMessage: It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited: 3 classes for ₹999 (Kenkere ₹699), birthday party class included. Love it? The ₹999 comes off your first month. Decide fast and you get to hit the big red buzzer.
offerBank.commercialJob: Bring April’s traffic in through a party, and convert it inside 72 hours.
offerBank.logic: A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

offerBank.kpi: Pass → member (target 35%); buzzer hits (bought within 9 hours).

offerBank.name: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work
offerBank.offerDetails: Lapsed 61 days–3 years get an obituary postcard (“Here lies a perfectly good plank”). It is the ticket to the candle-lit Séance Class on Thu 15 Apr. Come back on the standard 15% on 1 Month, a 12-class pack or 3 Months, plus a bonus for every year since your first class (max 3): +1 class on packs, +1 day on unlimited. Photo at the Back From the Dead frame; your row at the Throwback Reunion (Sat 24 Apr).
offerBank.headline: We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.

offerBank.customerMessage: Bride squad, assemble: get 4 or more of you together and your 12-class packs are 12% off each, plus a private Squad Class that ends on a Sangeet routine. Groom can come too. We don’t judge.
offerBank.commercialJob: Sell group packs into the wedding season, the one time in the year people train with a deadline.
offerBank.logic: November–December is shaadi season: brides, bridesmaids and families are motivated and arrive in groups. A group rate recruits several newcomers in one conversation, and the hosted class is time we already have, not cash.
offerBank.rules: 4+ buyers on the same day, at least 2 new to P57. 12% cash + hosted class at list ≈ 18.7% (Kenkere 19.8%). No stacking.
offerBank.kpi: Squads formed; new buyers from squads (target 50% of squad members).

offerBank.name: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January)
offerBank.offerDetails: Renew in December, 3 Months at 12% (₹50,912 / ₹37,145), 6 Months at 15% (₹96,658 / ₹69,883) or Annual at the standard 20%, and take home a 12-door P57 Advent-ure Calendar. One door a week from 3 Jan 2028: 3 guest passes, 2 smoothies, a 30-min virtual private, 2 extra days, a freeze, grip socks, a front-row reservation, a playlist pick and one golden door. Worth ≈₹4,000 Mumbai / ₹3,000 Bengaluru at list. Pop-ups: 10-class pack at 10% + a 3-door mini calendar (₹7,655).
offerBank.headline: An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.
offerBank.customerMessage: An advent calendar you open in January, when you need it most: renew for 3, 6 or 12 months in December and get 12 doors of perks, one a week from 3 Jan. Guest passes, a private, smoothies and a golden door.
offerBank.commercialJob: Renew December’s book onto long plans and get Q1 attendance built in.
offerBank.logic: January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.
offerBank.rules: 3M 18.9% / 6M 18.5% / annual 21.8% effective (calendar at list). Doors expire 31 Mar 2028; one calendar per renewal.
offerBank.kpi: December renewal yield; Q1 2028 visits of calendar holders vs others.

offerBank.name: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional)
offerBank.offerDetails: Sun 26–Mon 27 Dec only: 12-class packs at 20% off: Mumbai ₹15,750 (list ₹19,688), Kenkere ₹10,500 (₹13,125); pop-ups 10-class pack at 20% (₹6,804). Two per person; buy now, start whenever January starts for you.
offerBank.headline: Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.
offerBank.customerMessage: Boxing Day, gloves optional: 12-class packs are 20% off on 26–27 Dec only. Stock up before the January rush. Two per person.
offerBank.commercialJob: Bank January’s pack demand in the quietest week of the year.
offerBank.logic: The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.
offerBank.rules: Spot offer, 20% cash. Two per person. 26–27 Dec only.
offerBank.kpi: Packs sold in 48 hours; January visits on Boxing Day packs.

offerBank.name: Resolution Insurance (Claim Approved)
offerBank.offerDetails: Buy in December, start any day 1–10 Jan 2028. Newcomers: 1 Month at the standard 15% (₹17,203 / ₹12,406) with Resolution Insurance: no late-cancel fees all January, one “life happens” freeze, and a trainer call if you miss 3 booked classes, to rebuild your week. Members can gift the same plan or buy 3 Months at 15% starting in January.
offerBank.headline: Insure your resolution before you make it. Claim approved.
offerBank.customerMessage: Insure your resolution before you make it: buy your first month now, start any day 1–10 January, and January’s late-cancel fees are on us. Plus a freeze for when life happens. Claim approved.
offerBank.commercialJob: Sell January memberships in December and protect the first month.
offerBank.logic: Most January resolutions fail in week two. Cover for the usual excuses (late cancels, a bad week) costs little and is exactly what a nervous December buyer needs to hear.
offerBank.rules: Standard 15% only. Start date 1–10 Jan 2028. Cover applies to January only.
offerBank.kpi: Pre-sold January starts; January attendance of insured buyers.

offerBank.name: 11.11: Treat Yourself, Not Your Ex
offerBank.offerDetails: Thu 11 Nov, 11:11 am to 10:11 pm only: an 8-class pack at 20% off: Mumbai ₹10,500 (list ₹13,125), Kenkere ₹6,972 (₹8,715), pop-ups ₹5,544 (₹6,930). One per person, usual validity, members and newcomers alike.
offerBank.headline: 11.11. Eleven hours. Treat yourself, not your ex.
offerBank.customerMessage: 11.11: for eleven hours, treat yourself, not your ex. 8-class packs at 20% off from 11:11 am to 10:11 pm. One per person. Your ex isn’t invited.
offerBank.commercialJob: Add a single loud sales day to a quiet month without touching membership prices.
offerBank.logic: Singles’ Day is now a shopping date in India. A one-day pack price brings in fence-sitters and members topping up, at a discount that never reaches memberships.
offerBank.rules: Spot offer, 20% cash. One per person. 11:11 am–10:11 pm on 11 Nov only.
offerBank.kpi: Packs sold in 11 hours; pack buyers → membership by January.

offerBank.name: The Ex-Files: Season Finale
offerBank.offerDetails: Lapsed 90+ days: 1 Month or a 12-class pack at 10% (₹18,215 / ₹13,136), or 3 Months at 15% (₹49,177 / ₹35,879), plus a plus-one guest pass to the NYE Countdown Class (Fri 31 Dec, 11 am). Pop-ups: 8-class pack at 5% + a plus-one class (₹6,584).
offerBank.headline: Every great series needs a finale. Yours is a comeback.
offerBank.customerMessage: The Ex-Files: Season Finale. Before 2027 ends, one last episode: come back for 10% off (15% on 3 months) and bring a plus-one to our NYE Countdown Class.
offerBank.commercialJob: Reactivate long-lapsed clients before the January price of a fresh start.
offerBank.logic: People who come back in December arrive in January already in the habit. The plus-one turns a returner into a referral at the busiest social week of the year.
offerBank.rules: Lapsed 90+ days. 1M 19.6% / 3M 18.4% effective with the guest pass at list.
offerBank.kpi: Reactivations; plus-ones who buy in January.

offerBank.name: Same Time Next Week
offerBank.offerDetails: Pop-up regulars whose pack is running out take the same pack again at 15%: Copper + Cloves 10-class ₹7,229 (list ₹8,505) or 8-class ₹5,891 (list ₹6,930), with one extra week of validity. Bought before the old pack expires.
offerBank.headline: Your pack is nearly out. Same one again, 15% less.
offerBank.customerMessage: You're nearly out of classes. Take the same pack again at 15% off — ₹7,229 for ten at Copper + Cloves, ₹5,891 for eight — and we’ll add a week of validity so none of them go to waste.
offerBank.commercialJob: Hold the pop-up renewal rate with a mechanic that works in a month with no moment to hang an offer on.
offerBank.logic: The pop-ups sell class packs, not memberships, so renewal is a repurchase decision rather than an expiry date. Four of the twelve months carried a renewal target with no renewal offer in the catalogue; this is the standing one.
offerBank.rules: 15% off the pack, inside the cap. One per client per pack expiry. The extra week of validity has no cash value.
offerBank.kpi: Packs repurchased within 14 days of running out (target 55%); share of pop-up renewal revenue with an offer behind it.

offerBank.name: The Gift They Won’t Regift
offerBank.offerDetails: A boxed gift for someone new: Mumbai ₹2,499 (2 classes in any format + grip socks + ₹1,000 off a first membership), Kenkere ₹1,799 (2 Barre classes + socks + ₹750 off), pop-ups ₹1,199 (1 class + socks + ₹400 off). The credit is valid within 14 days of class 2, on top of the standard 15%. Offices buying 10+ boxes get 10% off the boxes and a hosted team class.
offerBank.headline: The one gift that doesn’t end up in next year’s Secret Santa.
offerBank.customerMessage: The gift they won’t regift: 2 classes, grip socks and ₹1,000 off their first membership, in a box that looks expensive. Buying for the office? 10+ boxes get 10% off and a team class.
offerBank.commercialJob: Turn December gifting into January newcomers.
offerBank.logic: A gift arrives with a friend’s endorsement, which is why gifted and referred clients convert far better than ad leads. The credit only pays out when the recipient buys.
offerBank.rules: Credited intro product (acquisition cost). On conversion: 1 Month at 15% less the credit ≈ 20% effective. Recipient must be new to P57.
offerBank.kpi: Boxes sold; boxes redeemed by 31 Jan; recipient → member (target 30%).

Pop-ups: a 9-class pack at ₹6,499 in the same windows.
offerBank.headline: Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.

months.name: January
months.objective: Turn New Year intent into paid commitments that are active on 1 Feb; re-up the annuals due Dec–Feb; test the 3-for-2 newcomer pack.
months.strategy:
Resolutions with Receipts.

Commercial job: Turn New Year intent into paid commitments that are active on 1 Feb; re-up the annuals due Dec–Feb; test the 3-for-2 newcomer pack.

Spot: The 57-Hour Hangover Sale (“Hungover? Same. 1 month unlimited, flat ₹15,000. 57 hours only.”). January is the strongest non-April month in Mumbai (Jan-26: Kwality ₹27.4L, Bandra ₹20.0L; Kenkere ₹11.1L). A capped spot price creates urgency without training clients to wait — only 57 units per city, so the maximum discount exposure is ~₹3.0L in Mumbai and ~₹2.6L in Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Third Time's the Charm (“First class: awkward. Second: better. Third: hooked. 3 classes for the price of 2.”). 60.6% of first-timers never take a 2nd class. Purchase within 60 days by month-1 visits: 0 return visits 10.8%, 1 → 43.9%, 2 → 73.3%, 3–4 → 88.6%. The 2-for-1 route converts 20.8% (Bandra 17%). A third class moves people into the 73–89% band.

Renewal: The Baker's Dozen (“12 months is so 2026. Renew your annual and get 13.”). Annual is Kwality's #1 product (32 units, ₹51.6L in the last 12 months) and Bandra's #3 (15 units, ₹23.8L). The ANN-2026-25%-KH code gave away ₹9.7L at a flat 25%; this gives less cash away (≈21.5% effective) and adds time, which costs little at spare capacity.

Lapsed: U Up? It's 2027. (“U up? Your mat's been asking about you.”). Bandra is reactivation-led (3,209 lapsed vs 5,065 renewed membership records). Renewal climbs with usage: Bandra members using <50% of sessions renew 49–58% vs 82% at 75%+. The bonus is only paid for attendance that predicts the next renewal.
months.notes: Build: 56 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹4.8L; 41 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹9.0L; 29 winbacks = ₹3.2L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.7L. Offers carry ₹12.7L (72% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 52% CRM status, trial→member 21.6%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: February
months.objective: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.
months.strategy:
Red Flags, Green Flags.

Commercial job: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.

Newcomer: Blind Date (No Catfishing) (“Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.”). Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.

Referral: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind) (“Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.

Renewal: Put a Ring On It (“If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.”). Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.

Lapsed: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule (“It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.”). Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
months.notes: Build: 52 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹4.4L; 38 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹8.3L; 27 winbacks = ₹2.9L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.6L. Offers carry ₹12.5L (77% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 52% CRM status, trial→member 21.6%) — not invented lifts.

months.strategy:
Cloud Nine — 9 Years of Physique 57.

Commercial job: Flagship month: win on excitement and economics. Two products that exist only in April (the 9-Month Lease and the 9-Class Pack), a 9:09 flash, a wheel you can double, numbered Club Nine annuals and a month of events, with no offer above 25% effective (cash ≤20% except annuals, the flash and the bulk pack). Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.

Upgrade: Moving In Together (The 9-Month Lease) (“Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. 99 keys. No second batch.”). A numbered, one-month-only product gives people a reason to buy now without cutting the price of the core memberships. April 2026 was bought with 40–48% codes; scarcity sells the long plan at 17.5–20% instead.

Renewal: Club Nine: The Founders’ Table (“Nine numbered seats per studio. Founder perks for a year.”). Annual buyers are the most valuable members in the book; a numbered seat with doubled perks costs less than a deeper price and gives them something to show off.

Renewal: Spin Class (Literally) (“Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.”). Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Party Crasher Pass (“It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited. 3 classes for ₹999.”). A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

Lapsed: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work (“We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.”). Lapsed clients already know the product; what they need is a moment and a reason that is not just a discount. A personal postcard with a dated class beats a generic reminder.

Referral: Plus One, Plus Nine (“Bring a friend, get 9 days. Bring three, get a month.”). Referrals convert at 22–76% against 3.8–5.7% for website leads. A tier at three friends gives the super-connectors a reason to keep going.

Spot: The 9:09 Panic Attack (“Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.”). A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. The floor price (23.7% / 24.0%) sits inside the 25% spot cap, and plan revenue is counted at the floor.

Upgrade: The Cloud Nine 90 (“Ninety classes. One year. Zero commitment issues.”). The Anniversary Big 85 Flex sold 4 times at Kemps Corner and once at Kenkere House in April 2026; this replaces it at a price inside the bulk cap.
months.notes: Build: 106 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹8.9L; 77 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹16.8L; 54 winbacks = ₹5.9L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹1.3L. months.strategy:
Book the Studio + Rain Check.

Commercial job: Studio bookouts and corporate bulk as new channels; protect monsoon renewals; bring lapsed clients back before August.

Bookout: Kitty Party, But Make It Cardio (“Kitty party, but make it cardio.”). Hosted classes are a top lead source (Kwality 394, Bandra 353, Kenkere 281 leads) but convert only 4.6–6.1%. A paid bookout has a host who brings warm friends and pays for the room.

Lapsed: Gone With the Wind, Back With the Rain (“Left us in the summer heat? Come back for the monsoon.”). An event with a start date beats a generic reminder. Freezes answer the monsoon objection at no cash cost.

months.strategy:
Azaadi From Average.

Commercial job: Recruit whole friend groups on Friendship Day; sell annuals over Freedom Weekend with a 2028 price lock instead of a deeper discount; remove the commitment objection for newcomers with a break-up clause; protect the festive-season renewal book with freezes. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit, never to a class count.

Newcomer: No Strings Attached (“Commitment issues? Same. Here’s a membership with a break-up clause.”). Clients with 5+ visits in month one buy again at 93.5%. A break-up clause costs almost nothing (few use it) and answers the objection the desk hears most: “what if I can’t keep it up?”.

Spot: Price Ki Azaadi (Freedom From Price Hikes) (“Freedom from price hikes. Lock your 2028 renewal at 2027 prices.”). A price lock costs nothing in 2027 and answers the renewal-price objection a year early. It sells the annual on certainty, not depth, and every lock is a 2028 renewal already in the book.

Referral: Squad Goals, Squat Goals (“Your squad. Our studio. Matching socks, obviously.”). Referrals convert at 22–76%; friends who start together come together. A free group class lowers the bar for the nervous friend, and the member is paid only when someone buys.

Renewal: Freedom to Pause (Not Quit) (“Pause for Ganpati. Pause for Diwali. Just don’t quit.”). Members lapse in Sep–Nov when travel breaks the habit. A freeze keeps them paying and coming back instead of cancelling; freezes have no cash cost, so the cash discount stays at the standard 15%.
months.notes: Build: 82 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹6.9L; 60 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹13.0L; 42 winbacks = ₹4.6L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹1.0L. Offers carry ₹19.0L (74% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 52% CRM status, trial→member 21.6%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: September
months.focus: The Comeback (winback month) + 57 Days to Diwali
months.objective: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.
months.strategy:
The Comeback + 57 Days to Diwali.

Commercial job: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.

Lapsed: We Need to Talk (“We need to talk. Not like that — we just miss you.”). These clients bought big before; a long plan at a serious price fits them. A personal call converts better than a broadcast.

Lapsed: New Phone, Who Dis? (“New phone, who dis? (It's us. Your favourite class.)”). A free first step lowers the barrier; the 7-day window keeps the decision fast. The freeze has no cash cost.

Newcomer: Glow-Up or Give Back (“57 days to Diwali. Glow up, or we give back.”). New clients' first 60-day spend averages ₹11,150 at Kwality, ₹8,411 at Bandra and ₹6,747 at Kenkere — under one month's list price. A 2-month bundle doubles it; the 30-class condition makes the guarantee rarely paid.

Renewal: Lock It Before the Laddoos (“Lock it before the laddoos.”). October–December are troughs (Kwality Nov-25 ₹18.5L; Bandra Oct-25 ₹10.2L). Locking 3M before the festive season protects the base.
months.notes: Build: 58 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹4.9L; 42 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹9.2L; 29 winbacks = ₹3.2L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.7L. Offers carry ₹13.5L (75% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 52% CRM status, trial→member 21.6%) — not invented lifts.

months.strategy:
Shaadi Season (and a Very Black Friday).

Commercial job: Sell group packs into the wedding season; bring lapsed clients back before the baraat; one loud 11-hour pack day on 11.11; and a Black Friday that moves renewals onto long plans with a mystery bonus instead of a deeper price.

Newcomer: Bride Squad, Assemble (Groom Can Come Too) (“Four of you, one wedding, zero excuses. Squad rates inside.”). November–December is shaadi season: brides, bridesmaids and families are motivated and arrive in groups. A group rate recruits several newcomers in one conversation, and the hosted class is time we already have, not cash.

Lapsed: Shaadi Mein Zaroor Aana (Come Back Before the Baraat) (“Shaadi mein zaroor aana. And to class before that.”). An event with a date beats a generic reminder, and the wedding season is the date. The socks and the class cost little and give a returner a reason to post.

Spot: 11.11: Treat Yourself, Not Your Ex (“11.11. Eleven hours. Treat yourself, not your ex.”). Singles’ Day is now a shopping date in India. A one-day pack price brings in fence-sitters and members topping up, at a discount that never reaches memberships.

Renewal: Black Friday Blind Box (No Duds) (“Black Friday, but every box is a winner. We checked.”). Black Friday discounts train members to wait. A mystery bonus keeps the cash discount at the standard ladder (10/15/20%) and makes opening the box the content.
months.notes: Build: 44 new buyers × ₹8,411 first-60-day spend = ₹3.7L; 32 renewals × ₹21,797 = ₹6.9L; 22 winbacks = ₹2.4L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.5L. Offers carry ₹8.8L (65% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 52% CRM status, trial→member 21.6%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: December
months.objective: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.
months.strategy:
Party Season Survival Guide.

Commercial job: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.

Renewal: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January) (“An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.”). January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.

Spot: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional) (“Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.”). The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.

Newcomer: Resolution Insurance (Claim Approved) (“Insure your resolution before you make it. Claim approved.”). Most January resolutions fail in week two. Cover for the usual excuses (late cancels, a bad week) costs little and is exactly what a nervous December buyer needs to hear.

months.name: February
months.objective: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.
months.strategy:
Red Flags, Green Flags.

Commercial job: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.

Newcomer: Blind Date (No Catfishing) (“Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.”). Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.

Referral: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind) (“Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.

Renewal: Put a Ring On It (“If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.”). Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.

Lapsed: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule (“It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.”). Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
months.notes: Build: 55 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.2L; 60 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹14.1L; 27 winbacks = ₹3.1L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.3L. Offers carry ₹19.3L (75% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

Commercial job: Hold the March trough: widen members' formats, use Women's Day for Bandra Lab acquisition, stop March expiries waiting for April, fix Bengaluru's second-visit leak.

months.strategy:
Cloud Nine — 9 Years of Physique 57.

Commercial job: Flagship month: win on excitement and economics. Two products that exist only in April (the 9-Month Lease and the 9-Class Pack), a 9:09 flash, a wheel you can double, numbered Club Nine annuals and a month of events, with no offer above 25% effective (cash ≤20% except annuals, the flash and the bulk pack). Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.

Upgrade: Moving In Together (The 9-Month Lease) (“Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. 99 keys. No second batch.”). A numbered, one-month-only product gives people a reason to buy now without cutting the price of the core memberships. April 2026 was bought with 40–48% codes; scarcity sells the long plan at 17.5–20% instead.

Renewal: Club Nine: The Founders’ Table (“Nine numbered seats per studio. Founder perks for a year.”). Annual buyers are the most valuable members in the book; a numbered seat with doubled perks costs less than a deeper price and gives them something to show off.

Renewal: Spin Class (Literally) (“Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.”). Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Party Crasher Pass (“It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited. 3 classes for ₹999.”). A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

Lapsed: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work (“We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.”). Lapsed clients already know the product; what they need is a moment and a reason that is not just a discount. A personal postcard with a dated class beats a generic reminder.

Referral: Plus One, Plus Nine (“Bring a friend, get 9 days. Bring three, get a month.”). Referrals convert at 22–76% against 3.8–5.7% for website leads. A tier at three friends gives the super-connectors a reason to keep going.

Spot: The 9:09 Panic Attack (“Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.”). A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. The floor price (23.7% / 24.0%) sits inside the 25% spot cap, and plan revenue is counted at the floor.

Upgrade: The Cloud Nine 90 (“Ninety classes. One year. Zero commitment issues.”). The Anniversary Big 85 Flex sold 4 times at Kemps Corner and once at Kenkere House in April 2026; this replaces it at a price inside the bulk cap.
months.notes: Build: 129 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹14.4L; 141 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹33.0L; 63 winbacks = ₹7.2L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹5.4L. Offers carry ₹45.1L (75% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: May
months.focus: Students home for the holidays + Mother's Day
months.objective: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.
months.strategy:
Home for the Holidays.

Commercial job: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.

Newcomer: Mom Said Get Off the Couch (“Home for the summer and Mom's already said 'do something'?”). Weekday 10–12 and weekend 4–7 pm run 27–41% full; the marginal cost of a seat there is near zero. Students arriving home in May are a predictable, untapped audience.

Newcomer: Group Project (Finally, Everyone Pulls Their Weight) (“Group projects: usually one person does all the work. Not here.”). Bulk purchase is one of the few places 25% is allowed. Groups attend together (higher usage → higher renewal) and bring four new names per sale.

Newcomer: Mom-entum (“She carried you for 9 months. You can carry her to class.”). Duos with a booked second class convert best; Mother's Day gives a reason. The perk is a shared session, not a bigger discount.

Renewal: Don't Ghost Us After the Party (“Great party. Now show up 8 times in May.”). 2026 anniversary-code buyers renewed at only 24.5%. Attendance in the month after purchase is the best predictor of renewal; the reward is earned by it.
months.notes: Build: 62 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.9L; 68 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹15.9L; 30 winbacks = ₹3.5L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.6L. Offers carry ₹13.8L (48% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: September
months.focus: The Comeback (winback month) + 57 Days to Diwali
months.objective: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.
months.strategy:
The Comeback + 57 Days to Diwali.

Commercial job: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.

Lapsed: We Need to Talk (“We need to talk. Not like that — we just miss you.”). These clients bought big before; a long plan at a serious price fits them. A personal call converts better than a broadcast.

Lapsed: New Phone, Who Dis? (“New phone, who dis? (It's us. Your favourite class.)”). A free first step lowers the barrier; the 7-day window keeps the decision fast. The freeze has no cash cost.

Newcomer: Glow-Up or Give Back (“57 days to Diwali. Glow up, or we give back.”). New clients' first 60-day spend averages ₹11,150 at Kwality, ₹8,411 at Bandra and ₹6,747 at Kenkere — under one month's list price. A 2-month bundle doubles it; the 30-class condition makes the guarantee rarely paid.

Renewal: Lock It Before the Laddoos (“Lock it before the laddoos.”). October–December are troughs (Kwality Nov-25 ₹18.5L; Bandra Oct-25 ₹10.2L). Locking 3M before the festive season protects the base.
months.notes: Build: 85 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹9.5L; 93 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹21.8L; 41 winbacks = ₹4.8L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹3.6L. months.name: November
months.theme: Shaadi Season (and a Very Black Friday)
months.objective: Sell group packs into the wedding season; bring lapsed clients back before the baraat; one loud 11-hour pack day on 11.11; and a Black Friday that moves renewals onto long plans with a mystery bonus instead of a deeper price.
months.strategy:
Shaadi Season (and a Very Black Friday).

Commercial job: Sell group packs into the wedding season; bring lapsed clients back before the baraat; one loud 11-hour pack day on 11.11; and a Black Friday that moves renewals onto long plans with a mystery bonus instead of a deeper price.

Newcomer: Bride Squad, Assemble (Groom Can Come Too) (“Four of you, one wedding, zero excuses. Squad rates inside.”). November–December is shaadi season: brides, bridesmaids and families are motivated and arrive in groups. A group rate recruits several newcomers in one conversation, and the hosted class is time we already have, not cash.

Lapsed: Shaadi Mein Zaroor Aana (Come Back Before the Baraat) (“Shaadi mein zaroor aana. And to class before that.”). An event with a date beats a generic reminder, and the wedding season is the date. The socks and the class cost little and give a returner a reason to post.

Spot: 11.11: Treat Yourself, Not Your Ex (“11.11. Eleven hours. Treat yourself, not your ex.”). Singles’ Day is now a shopping date in India. A one-day pack price brings in fence-sitters and members topping up, at a discount that never reaches memberships.

Renewal: Black Friday Blind Box (No Duds) (“Black Friday, but every box is a winner. We checked.”). Black Friday discounts train members to wait. A mystery bonus keeps the cash discount at the standard ladder (10/15/20%) and makes opening the box the content.
months.notes: Build: 46 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹5.1L; 50 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹11.8L; 22 winbacks = ₹2.6L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹1.9L. Offers carry ₹13.8L (64% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: December
months.objective: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.
months.strategy:
Party Season Survival Guide.

Commercial job: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.

Renewal: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January) (“An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.”). January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.

Spot: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional) (“Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.”). The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.

Newcomer: Resolution Insurance (Claim Approved) (“Insure your resolution before you make it. Claim approved.”). Most January resolutions fail in week two. Cover for the usual excuses (late cancels, a bad week) costs little and is exactly what a nervous December buyer needs to hear.

Newcomer: The Gift They Won’t Regift (“The one gift that doesn’t end up in next year’s Secret Santa.”). A gift arrives with a friend’s endorsement, which is why gifted and referred clients convert far better than ad leads. The credit only pays out when the recipient buys.

Lapsed: The Ex-Files: Season Finale (“Every great series needs a finale. Yours is a comeback.”). People who come back in December arrive in January already in the habit. The plus-one turns a returner into a referral at the busiest social week of the year.
months.notes: Build: 75 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹8.4L; 82 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹19.2L; 37 winbacks = ₹4.2L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹3.1L. Offers carry ₹26.0L (74% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

Resolutions with Receipts.

Commercial job: Turn New Year intent into paid commitments that are active on 1 Feb; re-up the annuals due Dec–Feb; test the 3-for-2 newcomer pack.

Spot: The 57-Hour Hangover Sale (“Hungover? Same. 1 month unlimited, flat ₹15,000. 57 hours only.”). January is the strongest non-April month in Mumbai (Jan-26: Kwality ₹27.4L, Bandra ₹20.0L; Kenkere ₹11.1L). A capped spot price creates urgency without training clients to wait — only 57 units per city, so the maximum discount exposure is ~₹3.0L in Mumbai and ~₹2.6L in Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Third Time's the Charm (“First class: awkward. Second: better. Third: hooked. 3 classes for the price of 2.”). 60.6% of first-timers never take a 2nd class. Purchase within 60 days by month-1 visits: 0 return visits 10.8%, 1 → 43.9%, 2 → 73.3%, 3–4 → 88.6%. The 2-for-1 route converts 20.8% (Bandra 17%). A third class moves people into the 73–89% band.

Renewal: The Baker's Dozen (“12 months is so 2026. Renew your annual and get 13.”). Annual is Kwality's #1 product (32 units, ₹51.6L in the last 12 months) and Bandra's #3 (15 units, ₹23.8L). The ANN-2026-25%-KH code gave away ₹9.7L at a flat 25%; this gives less cash away (≈21.5% effective) and adds time, which costs little at spare capacity.

Lapsed: U Up? It's 2027. (“U up? Your mat's been asking about you.”). Bandra is reactivation-led (3,209 lapsed vs 5,065 renewed membership records). Renewal climbs with usage: Bandra members using <50% of sessions renew 49–58% vs 82% at 75%+. The bonus is only paid for attendance that predicts the next renewal.

months.name: February
months.objective: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.
months.strategy:
Red Flags, Green Flags.

Commercial job: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.

Newcomer: Blind Date (No Catfishing) (“Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.”). Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.

Referral: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind) (“Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.

Renewal: Put a Ring On It (“If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.”). Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.

Lapsed: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule (“It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.”). Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
months.notes: Build: 48 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹3.3L; 33 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹5.1L; 6 winbacks = ₹0.6L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.7L. Offers carry ₹5.6L (59% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.strategy:
Cloud Nine — 9 Years of Physique 57.

Commercial job: Flagship month: win on excitement and economics. Two products that exist only in April (the 9-Month Lease and the 9-Class Pack), a 9:09 flash, a wheel you can double, numbered Club Nine annuals and a month of events, with no offer above 25% effective (cash ≤20% except annuals, the flash and the bulk pack). Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.

Upgrade: Moving In Together (The 9-Month Lease) (“Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. 99 keys. No second batch.”). A numbered, one-month-only product gives people a reason to buy now without cutting the price of the core memberships. April 2026 was bought with 40–48% codes; scarcity sells the long plan at 17.5–20% instead.

Renewal: Club Nine: The Founders’ Table (“Nine numbered seats per studio. Founder perks for a year.”). Annual buyers are the most valuable members in the book; a numbered seat with doubled perks costs less than a deeper price and gives them something to show off.

Renewal: Spin Class (Literally) (“Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.”). Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Party Crasher Pass (“It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited. 3 classes for ₹999.”). A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

Lapsed: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work (“We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.”). Lapsed clients already know the product; what they need is a moment and a reason that is not just a discount. A personal postcard with a dated class beats a generic reminder.

Referral: Plus One, Plus Nine (“Bring a friend, get 9 days. Bring three, get a month.”). Referrals convert at 22–76% against 3.8–5.7% for website leads. A tier at three friends gives the super-connectors a reason to keep going.

Spot: The 9:09 Panic Attack (“Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.”). A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. The floor price (23.7% / 24.0%) sits inside the 25% spot cap, and plan revenue is counted at the floor.
months.notes: Build: 76 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹5.1L; 52 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹8.0L; 10 winbacks = ₹0.9L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹1.1L. Offers carry ₹9.4L (62% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: May
months.focus: Students home for the holidays + Mother's Day
months.objective: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.
months.strategy:
Home for the Holidays.

Commercial job: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.

Newcomer: Mom Said Get Off the Couch (“Home for the summer and Mom's already said 'do something'?”). Weekday 10–12 and weekend 4–7 pm run 27–41% full; the marginal cost of a seat there is near zero. Students arriving home in May are a predictable, untapped audience.

Newcomer: Group Project (Finally, Everyone Pulls Their Weight) (“Group projects: usually one person does all the work. Not here.”). Bulk purchase is one of the few places 25% is allowed. Groups attend together (higher usage → higher renewal) and bring four new names per sale.

Newcomer: Mom-entum (“She carried you for 9 months. You can carry her to class.”). Duos with a booked second class convert best; Mother's Day gives a reason. The perk is a shared session, not a bigger discount.

Renewal: Don't Ghost Us After the Party (“Great party. Now show up 8 times in May.”). 2026 anniversary-code buyers renewed at only 24.5%. Attendance in the month after purchase is the best predictor of renewal; the reward is earned by it.
months.notes: Build: 57 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹3.9L; 39 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹6.0L; 8 winbacks = ₹0.7L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.8L. Offers carry ₹4.0L (35% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: September
months.focus: The Comeback (winback month) + 57 Days to Diwali
months.objective: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.
months.strategy:
The Comeback + 57 Days to Diwali.

Commercial job: Winback month: manager calls for high-value lapsed clients, fast comebacks for recent lapsers; a results-guarantee bundle; lock 3M plans before the festive dip.

Lapsed: We Need to Talk (“We need to talk. Not like that — we just miss you.”). These clients bought big before; a long plan at a serious price fits them. A personal call converts better than a broadcast.

Lapsed: New Phone, Who Dis? (“New phone, who dis? (It's us. Your favourite class.)”). A free first step lowers the barrier; the 7-day window keeps the decision fast. The freeze has no cash cost.

Newcomer: Glow-Up or Give Back (“57 days to Diwali. Glow up, or we give back.”). New clients' first 60-day spend averages ₹11,150 at Kwality, ₹8,411 at Bandra and ₹6,747 at Kenkere — under one month's list price. A 2-month bundle doubles it; the 30-class condition makes the guarantee rarely paid.

Renewal: Lock It Before the Laddoos (“Lock it before the laddoos.”). October–December are troughs (Kwality Nov-25 ₹18.5L; Bandra Oct-25 ₹10.2L). Locking 3M before the festive season protects the base.
months.notes: Build: 59 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹4.0L; 41 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹6.3L; 8 winbacks = ₹0.7L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.8L. Offers carry ₹7.6L (64% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: November
months.theme: Shaadi Season (and a Very Black Friday)
months.objective: Sell group packs into the wedding season; bring lapsed clients back before the baraat; one loud 11-hour pack day on 11.11; and a Black Friday that moves renewals onto long plans with a mystery bonus instead of a deeper price.
months.strategy:
Shaadi Season (and a Very Black Friday).

Commercial job: Sell group packs into the wedding season; bring lapsed clients back before the baraat; one loud 11-hour pack day on 11.11; and a Black Friday that moves renewals onto long plans with a mystery bonus instead of a deeper price.

Newcomer: Bride Squad, Assemble (Groom Can Come Too) (“Four of you, one wedding, zero excuses. Squad rates inside.”). November–December is shaadi season: brides, bridesmaids and families are motivated and arrive in groups. A group rate recruits several newcomers in one conversation, and the hosted class is time we already have, not cash.

Lapsed: Shaadi Mein Zaroor Aana (Come Back Before the Baraat) (“Shaadi mein zaroor aana. And to class before that.”). An event with a date beats a generic reminder, and the wedding season is the date. The socks and the class cost little and give a returner a reason to post.

Spot: 11.11: Treat Yourself, Not Your Ex (“11.11. Eleven hours. Treat yourself, not your ex.”). Singles’ Day is now a shopping date in India. A one-day pack price brings in fence-sitters and members topping up, at a discount that never reaches memberships.

Renewal: Black Friday Blind Box (No Duds) (“Black Friday, but every box is a winner. We checked.”). Black Friday discounts train members to wait. A mystery bonus keeps the cash discount at the standard ladder (10/15/20%) and makes opening the box the content.
months.notes: Build: 57 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹3.8L; 39 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹6.0L; 7 winbacks = ₹0.7L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.8L. Offers carry ₹4.6L (41% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: December
months.objective: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.
months.strategy:
Party Season Survival Guide.

Commercial job: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.

Renewal: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January) (“An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.”). January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.

Spot: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional) (“Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.”). The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.

Newcomer: Resolution Insurance (Claim Approved) (“Insure your resolution before you make it. Claim approved.”). Most January resolutions fail in week two. Cover for the usual excuses (late cancels, a bad week) costs little and is exactly what a nervous December buyer needs to hear.

Newcomer: The Gift They Won’t Regift (“The one gift that doesn’t end up in next year’s Secret Santa.”). A gift arrives with a friend’s endorsement, which is why gifted and referred clients convert far better than ad leads. The credit only pays out when the recipient buys.

Lapsed: The Ex-Files: Season Finale (“Every great series needs a finale. Yours is a comeback.”). People who come back in December arrive in January already in the habit. The plus-one turns a returner into a referral at the busiest social week of the year.
months.notes: Build: 42 new buyers × ₹6,747 first-60-day spend = ₹2.8L; 29 renewals × ₹15,422 = ₹4.4L; 6 winbacks = ₹0.5L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.6L. Offers carry ₹5.9L (71% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 36% CRM status, trial→member 18.7%) — not invented lifts.

months.name: February
months.objective: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.
months.strategy:
Red Flags, Green Flags.

Commercial job: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.

Newcomer: Blind Date (No Catfishing) (“Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.”). Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.

Referral: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind) (“Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.

Renewal: Put a Ring On It (“If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.”). Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.

Lapsed: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule (“It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.”). Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
months.notes: Build: 48 new buyers × ₹2,087 first-60-day spend = ₹1.0L; 11 renewals × ₹7,241 = ₹0.8L; 0 winbacks = ₹0.0L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.0L. Offers carry ₹0.6L (35% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 26% CRM status, trial→member 32.9%) — not invented lifts.

Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.
months.strategy:
Cloud Nine — 9 Years of Physique 57.

Commercial job: Flagship month: win on excitement and economics. Two products that exist only in April (the 9-Month Lease and the 9-Class Pack), a 9:09 flash, a wheel you can double, numbered Club Nine annuals and a month of events, with no offer above 25% effective (cash ≤20% except annuals, the flash and the bulk pack). Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.

Renewal: Spin Class (Literally) (“Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.”). Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Party Crasher Pass (“It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited. 3 classes for ₹999.”). A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

Lapsed: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work (“We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.”). Lapsed clients already know the product; what they need is a moment and a reason that is not just a discount. A personal postcard with a dated class beats a generic reminder.

Referral: Plus One, Plus Nine (“Bring a friend, get 9 days. Bring three, get a month.”). Referrals convert at 22–76% against 3.8–5.7% for website leads. A tier at three friends gives the super-connectors a reason to keep going.

Spot: The 9:09 Panic Attack (“Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.”). A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. The floor price (23.7% / 24.0%) sits inside the 25% spot cap, and plan revenue is counted at the floor.
months.notes: Build: 40 new buyers × ₹2,087 first-60-day spend = ₹0.8L; 9 renewals × ₹7,241 = ₹0.7L; 0 winbacks = ₹0.0L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.0L. Offers carry ₹1.0L (67% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 26% CRM status, trial→member 32.9%) — not invented lifts.

months.strategy:
Azaadi From Average.

Commercial job: Recruit whole friend groups on Friendship Day; sell annuals over Freedom Weekend with a 2028 price lock instead of a deeper discount; remove the commitment objection for newcomers with a break-up clause; protect the festive-season renewal book with freezes. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit, never to a class count.

Newcomer: No Strings Attached (“Commitment issues? Same. Here’s a membership with a break-up clause.”). Clients with 5+ visits in month one buy again at 93.5%. A break-up clause costs almost nothing (few use it) and answers the objection the desk hears most: “what if I can’t keep it up?”.

Referral: Squad Goals, Squat Goals (“Your squad. Our studio. Matching socks, obviously.”). Referrals convert at 22–76%; friends who start together come together. A free group class lowers the bar for the nervous friend, and the member is paid only when someone buys.

Renewal: Freedom to Pause (Not Quit) (“Pause for Ganpati. Pause for Diwali. Just don’t quit.”). Members lapse in Sep–Nov when travel breaks the habit. A freeze keeps them paying and coming back instead of cancelling; freezes have no cash cost, so the cash discount stays at the standard 15%.
months.notes: Build: 54 new buyers × ₹2,087 first-60-day spend = ₹1.1L; 12 renewals × ₹7,241 = ₹0.9L; 0 winbacks = ₹0.0L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹0.0L. Offers carry ₹0.8L (38% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 26% CRM status, trial→member 32.9%) — not invented lifts.

months.strategy:
Party Season Survival Guide.

Commercial job: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.

Renewal: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January) (“An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.”). January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.

Spot: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional) (“Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.”). The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.

Newcomer: The Gift They Won’t Regift (“The one gift that doesn’t end up in next year’s Secret Santa.”). A gift arrives with a friend’s endorsement, which is why gifted and referred clients convert far better than ad leads. The credit only pays out when the recipient buys.

Lapsed: The Ex-Files: Season Finale (“Every great series needs a finale. Yours is a comeback.”). People who come back in December arrive in January already in the habit. The plus-one turns a returner into a referral at the busiest social week of the year.

standardTrade.note: Full-price trade: memberships, packs and privates sold at list with no offer behind them. Owned by the studio manager and the front desk, not by a campaign. The plan does not model it offer by offer.

economics.reason: The plan models revenue and discount cost, not delivery cost. Contribution margin is computed by the offer engine from benefit costs; it is not filed in the plan.

assumptions: Offers carry ₹5,00,40,897 of the year (63%); ₹2,96,70,643 is expected at full price.
Full-price trade is not broken down by stream or product — it is the balance of each month’s target after the planned offers, owned by the studio manager.
Offer buyers are the campaign slice only. A month’s funnel needs more buyers than its offers name; the difference is full-price trade.
